newsitem.title: USA: UAL, GE, McDonnell to pay $15 million in crash suit.
newsitem.headline: UAL, GE, McDonnell to pay $15 million in crash suit.

text.p: UAL Corp., General Electric Co. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. have agreed to pay $15 million to an Illinois man whose wife and daughter were killed in a 1989 United Airlines crash, the plaintiffs attorney said Friday.
Robert Clifford, an attorney for Terry Brown, said the settlement was among the last from the crash in Sioux City, Iowa, that killed 112 of the 296 people on board.
The settlement was approved recently by Judge Donald O'Connell of the Circuit Court of Cook County, Ill.
More than 285 cases from the crash have been settled.
The amount of the settlement to be paid by each of the three defendants has not been determined as yet, Rick Kennedy, a spokesman for GE Aircraft Engines, said Friday.
A McDonnell Douglas spokesman said the three defendants face a separate suit to determine the percentage of the settlements each company will pay.
As part of the Brown suit, Kennedy said GE was prepared to acknowledge the defendants' corporate responsibility for the circumstances that led to the accident.
He stressed that GE did not admit to sole responsibility for the crash, which was caused by a crack in an aircraft engine fan disk that had not been detected in prior maintenance inspections.
A spokeswoman for UAL, parent of United Airlines, said the case was settled "to the satisifaction of both parties," referring to the airline and the plaintiff.
UAL's stock fell 37.5 cents to 45.75, GE rose $1.25 to $88.25 and McDonnell Douglas edged down 12.5 cents to $51.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
